# R394 v2 — historical Strata SYCL performance records recovered

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). This supplements, and does not overwrite, `research-historical-performance-regression-round394-v1.txt`. Read-only review of the supplied 409-message filtered session-statement extract, the committed SYCL docs, current quiet upstream-bench report, and pinned GitHub PR #6/#8 report and measurement files. No source edits, build, test, GPU/model/service/process operation, cleanup, or Git mutation was performed. No active 4331 log or protected prefill-gemm-only record was read. This report is the only new write.

## Correction to v1

V1 missed material Intel Arc B570 / Ryzen 5 5600X history because it focused on current bench/results and later B570 records. It was wrong to suggest that the higher rates were explained by unrelated NVIDIA/Windows results or to say no earlier B570 record existed. The filtered session extract identifies PR #6's same-condition 32K measurement and PR #8's 64K cache-release measurements. Their reports and run artifacts are pinned in the public Git history and contain much richer measurement details than the short session summaries. They are valid historical performance evidence with their original scope and limitations; they are not measurements to discard because the newer official client differs.

## PR #6: repeated 32K normal-wall comparison

The filtered session statement at `main-session-speed-statements-audit-v2.json` (2026-10-05T08:32:29.114Z) said 32K prefill improved 453→646 tok/s with matching output and PR #6 merged. The pinned PR is `https://github.com/yqYo1/Strata/pull/6`, title “perf(sycl): reuse expert layers across prompt chunks”, base `52d2f9f08f9ce66f34921e589407dc3294db4e5d`, head `d0c5dda0dc2e8d82458c4b0ff31c4cef44c40b32`. Its core implementation commit is `f263d87d44aa671d056c33e6c6b6b0635fc25b8c`; the run records are under `bench/results/2026-10-05-sycl-prefill-scaling/layer-major/` at that PR head.

The decisive quiet (no phase/transfer timers or diagnostic PLE preload) comparison is `layer-major/paired-normal-wall/summary.json`, with individual `baseline-p1/p2/p3/run.json` and `layer-major-p1/p2/p3/run.json`. It reports three alternating pairs, with pair 2 order reversed. Exact per-arm rates: baseline 453.3067, 453.2935, 453.2935 tok/s; layer-major 640.3414, 646.4646, 645.8480 tok/s. Median normal prefill wall fell from 72,288.7 ms to 50,736.4 ms, a 29.814% elapsed reduction. The same `binary_sha256` is `eae0f3ed824d13cf25033e7dc60d1f8e69bb770b0b764ea6600a9900969b7ed9`, and the fixture SHA in each run is `aea4383be22560c13bcdf3653215e1c6c4f1bbb24c472d4667b7fdc03df597a0`. The per-run fixture is the 64K coding stream prefix; each timed request consumed exactly 32,768 input tokens, emitted one greedy token (`--max-new 1`), and had matching complete 248,320-value first-logit head and output ID. The report says all six heads/output IDs matched.

Recorded recipe: IQ3_S Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model/packs, Arc B570 10 GiB, Ryzen 5 5600X, 128 GiB host RAM, oneAPI 2026.1 with selected compute runtime 26.35.39758.10, precise math, fixed max context 65,538, int8 KV, all K/V resident, 8,192-token prefill chunks, 128-slot per-layer cache, direct PLE reads with 16 I/O threads, preload disabled, expert-cache profile, five CPU workers, PCIe fraction zero, adaptive swaps zero, suffix draft zero, greedy sampling. The command also passed `--spec 2`; JSON `mtp` metadata is null. Preserve that argv as recorded; the one-token prefill measurement does not establish a decode-rate sample. Baseline has `STRATA_PREFILL_COMPACT=0`, `STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_MAJOR=0`, residual prefix 0; candidate has compact=2, layer-major=1 and the first 32,768 FP32 residual rows resident in GPU memory. This is a source/option A/B, not a stock-client current-versus-old comparison.

The mechanism matters: layer-major traverses all chunks for one layer before advancing, uploading its 512 quantized experts once per layer instead of repeating those uploads for each chunk. FP32 residual rows bridge layers while layer/chunk GEMM dimensions, dequantization, FP16 conversions and combine order are preserved. Compact scratch lowers workspace. The report states 50.292 GB expert traffic on the candidate versus 190.110 GB on baseline for the 32K case in its separate transfer record. The user-facing PR body calls out the paired normal-wall runs as all-output-matching, fully touched warm-table results and warns against combining them with earlier timings to claim an additional gain. This is credible measured evidence for this exact old recipe, not a 646 tok/s universal SYCL expectation.

The second old 32K candidate test has a separately documented issue: `layer-major/8k-chunk-long` is a transfer-instrumented one-shot and shows only 439.98 tok/s candidate vs 412.13 baseline at 32K. That row must not replace the three-pair normal-wall record; its transfer timings and diagnostic mode are explicitly different. This also illustrates why retained original records and timing definitions matter.

## PR #8: 64K, 4K-chunk decode-cache release

The filtered statement at 2026-10-05T11:21:36.069Z summarized cache policies at 64K/4K chunk as 520/533/540 tok/s and linked PR #8. Pinned PR is `https://github.com/yqYo1/Strata/pull/8`, title “feat(sycl): lend decode expert-cache VRAM to layer-major prefill”, base `f53d865afc9cb0423b787023f99f5ab1eb612851`, head `dd0f6e782e5a0ac3dab46ccd56ed711a4f1d5153`; the final correction commit is `dd0f6e7` and cache-release implementation commit is `f41b4022b6e5dd6f496928b74e9a02bf7bd7094a`. Its `bench/results/2026-10-05-sycl-prefill-scaling/cache-release/README.md`, `long-context/comparison.json`, `long-context/capacity-maxima/summary.json`, and per-run `run.json` files were read at the pinned PR head.

The source records 65,536 input tokens, 4,096 chunk, fixed 65,538-position K8/V8 context, 128 decode cache slots, same frozen JIT binary, IQ3_S, Arc B570 10 GiB / Ryzen 5 5600X / 128 GiB RAM, oneAPI 2026.1, precise math. Commands use the coding-context-64k fixture, `--max-new 1 --spec 2 --max-context 65538 --prefill 4096 --no-prefill-borrow --expert-cache 128 --kv int8 --expert-cache-per-layer --pool-workers 5 --pcie-frac 0 --adapt-swaps 0 --ple-io direct --greedy`; transfer diagnostics are on. `comparison.json` classifies the observations as single runs, not repeated medians. It gives:

- Retain cache with first 32,768 residual rows in GPU: 140,995.9 ms, 464.81 tok/s.
- Retain cache, largest fitting 57,344-row residual prefix: 126,097.3 ms, 519.73 tok/s.
- Release half cache, restore from RAM, 61,440 residual rows in GPU: 123,064.6 ms, 532.53 tok/s.
- Release full cache, restore from RAM, all 65,536 residual rows in GPU: 121,417.6 ms, 539.76 tok/s.
- Full release snapshot/rebuild RAM restore observations: 542.30/542.13 tok/s, respectively.

Every successful configuration has a finite complete first head and matching generated IDs; capacity refusals are retained. Full release decreases observed time by 3.7% from the largest fitting retained-cache prefix, but does not prove a repeated speed win among restore methods. These records are valuable single-case diagnostic evidence, not a repeated median and not comparable as a precise wall-rate difference with quiet PR #6's timer-free wall run. PR #8 body gives restoration mechanics and details separately: keep virtual address/graph or rebuild allocation/graphs; RAM restore uses existing arena; cache release is opt-in and defaults unchanged.

## Earlier short-context decode record

The filtered 2026-10-03T08:16:19.507Z final states the IQ3_S short-context configuration used context 512 and 128 generated tokens; repeated code generation median was 18.30 tok/s. It explicitly contrasts this with the prior Q2_0 code-generation 29.70 tok/s on the same workstation, but different model. This is a valid short-context historical decode rate and supports the user's concern that prefill/decode have both been faster in past contexts. It does not imply a long-context 70 tok/s SYCL run and must remain separate from prefill measurements. The contemporaneous report is `docs/SYCL_STATUS_2026-10-03.md` and detailed implementation report `docs/SYCL_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; short-context fixture, cache, MTP and timers differ from current 32K/24 stock rows.

## Current official client row and what is comparable

The current quiet COPY pair report was read at `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-fixed-history-logits-comparator-20261013/bench/results/2026-10-13-upstream-benchsh-quiet-copy-pair/REPORT.md`. Its source was 410904c99d273435b5302fa8976cc667d17957f2 / source-built DPC++7.1.1 and binary `b54579...`; same B570/5600X and IQ3_S, 8,192 chunk, 32,049 actual fresh read tokens, 24 generated output tokens, direct client engine timings, max context 262,144, int8 KV resident 32,768, no borrow/MTP/prompt reuse, five workers/tasks18, cache128/effective144. COPY0 samples prefill 407.5/408.0/403.0, median 407.5 tok/s; COPY1 478.0/470.8/474.8, median 474.8. Copy1 was selected as requested and sole arm option was `STRATA_COPY_ENGINE`; decode medians were 8.6 and 8.7, with overlapping ranges.

The older PR #6 32K comparison is the closest historical prefill benchmark: same machine/model label, same 8K chunks, fresh exact 32,768 tokens, and similar source-built Intel runtime. It establishes that a named earlier source/option recipe measured 453.29 baseline and 645.85 layer-major tok/s under a fixed 65,538 context, fully resident K/V, 1-token greedy output, no transfer/phase tracing. Current stock COPY0 is 407.5 and COPY1 is 474.8, but direct numerical deltas are not controlled comparisons: actual input differs (32,768 vs 32,049), timing path and generated length differ (direct custom GEN max-new1 vs API stock bench 24), configured context/KV policy differs (65,538 K8/V8 vs 262,144 with int8 resident 32,768), effective expert cache differs (128 vs 144), data stream and process/table warmup history differ, source and binary differ, and COPY is a current-only arm. Still, PR #6 is not “invalid”: its triple-paired recipe-specific speed result remains established evidence and its large layer-major advantage should be represented as a historical opt-in optimization result.

PR #8 is a separate 64K capacity/policy study (4K chunk, cache lending, transfer diagnostics) and has no current 64K official-bench counterpart. Do not compare its rates to the current 32K stock case as a regression ratio. Preserve the 520/533/540 values as recorded single-sample measurements with the specific VRAM policy and instrumentation noted.

## Source/option chronology evidence

PR #6 introduced and measured layer-major prompt traversal and compact scratch as explicit opt-ins. PR #8 built on that source and added full/partial decode-cache release/restoration for 64K capacity. The current measured 410904c stock server config does not enable those old controls; the tested current source tree at 6035c4f92bf87362d7e55051ae1375b9befba89e exposes no `STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_MAJOR`, `STRATA_PREFILL_COMPACT`, or `STRATA_PREFILL_RELEASE_CACHE` in the production prefill source/header (the only current `STRATA_PREFILL_COMPACT*` match is a separate `STRATA_PREFILL_COMPACT_MOE_SCRATCH` flag). This proves the measured/current-source path is not running PR #6/8's layer-major/cache-release implementation. It does not, by itself, prove whether this source port deliberately replaced the route with a faster equivalent, or identify the exact commit where behavior disappeared.

Consequently, the strongest causal explanation presently supported is a concrete source/option loss: the earlier 32K winner used `compact=2 + layer_major=1 + 32K residual GPU prefix` and current measurement has no corresponding route. The old-vs-current rate delta remains confounded by workload and context. The 64K option cannot be a fair same-context comparison until the old and new source have a 64K workload with identical token stream, context/KV, cache, batch, transfer instrumentation off, input/output/horizon, and timer definition. Full source genealogy and the precise removal/port commit are delegated to the separate Git/source audit; do not guess a culprit among kernels or CPU flags from these measurements.

## Minimal verification that preserves the old claim

Once the current run is closed, the smallest decisive sequence is: (1) repeat the PR #6 exact 32,768 token fixture/prompt, 65,538 K8/V8 context, 8K chunks, cache128, direct PLE, exact CPU/env/affinity and greedy 1-token custom GEN on current source; compare current's equivalent default route with a reviewed restoration/port of the old layer-major recipe only if source review identifies a safe matched implementation. Preserve each original old pair and new sample; report all individual values and output IDs/full-head checks. (2) Separately repeat the PR #8 exact 65,536/4K/cache policy measurements with transfer tracing disabled for wall comparison, same K8/V8 context and original cache release arms; retain the existing instrumented sample as diagnostic evidence. (3) If only stock `bench.sh` is approved, run its unchanged 32K/24 case as a new series; it supplements but does not replace custom GEN history. Do not transform the old measured rates by arithmetic to predict current.
